metadata.title: Image to 3D Relief - Free Online Tool
metadata.description: Free online tool to turn any photo into a 3D relief. Preview in 3D and export GLB or STL. No signup, fully private — processing happens in your browser.

image-to-relief.title: Image to 3D Relief
image-to-relief.description: Turn any photo into a 3D relief based on its brightness. Preview the result in full 3D and export as GLB or STL — all in your browser.

whatIs.title: What is an image-to-3D relief tool?
body: This tool turns any photo into a 3D relief: it maps the image's brightness onto a mesh so bright areas stand out, then lets you preview the result with full 3D controls and export it as GLB (viewers/game engines) or STL (3D printing). Everything runs locally in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

howTo.title: How to use
items: Upload an image (JPG, PNG or WebP).
Adjust grid resolution, relief strength and smoothing, then click Generate 3D.
Preview the mesh (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom), then download GLB or STL.

tips.title: Tips
items: Images with strong contrast produce more dramatic reliefs.
Increase smoothing to reduce noise on detailed photos.
For 3D printing, choose STL — the model is automatically laid flat for slicing.

faqs.question: How is the 3D relief generated?
faqs.answer: The tool reads each pixel's brightness (luminance) and lifts the mesh height accordingly — bright areas rise, dark areas stay low. Parameters let you control resolution, height and smoothing.

faqs.question: What's the difference between GLB and STL?
faqs.answer: GLB is a general 3D format for viewers and game engines. STL is the standard format for 3D printing and is exported pre-oriented flat.

faqs.question: Is my image uploaded?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens in your browser; your image never leaves your device.

faqs.question: Why does my result look flat?
faqs.answer: Low-contrast images produce subtle reliefs. Try increasing relief strength, lowering smoothing, or using a photo with stronger lighting contrast.

labels.previewHint: Drag to rotate · Scroll to zoom

metadata.title: ID Photo Generator

faqs.question: Is this ID photo generator free?
faqs.answer: Yes, completely free. No registration, no watermarks, no hidden fees. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.question: What ID sizes are supported?
faqs.answer: We support US passport/visa (2×2 in), EU/UK passport (35×45 mm), China passport (33×48 mm), Japan passport (45×35 mm), 1×1 inch (25×25 mm), small ID (30×40 mm), plus Chinese 1-inch (25×35 mm) and 2-inch (35×49 mm) photos. All sizes output at 300 DPI.

faqs.question: Can I change the background color?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose white, blue, red or gray — the chosen color is placed behind your photo.

faqs.question: What if my photo isn't perfectly centered?
faqs.answer: Use the X/Y offset sliders to move the photo and the zoom slider to control how large the face appears.

faqs.question: Is my photo uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: No. The AI background removal and all rendering happen entirely in your browser using WebAssembly — your photo never leaves your device.

whatIs.title: What is an ID photo generator?

Upload a portrait, and the AI removes the background so you can place your face on any official background color (white, blue, red or gray). Pick one of the international sizes — all rendered at 300 DPI print quality — adjust zoom and position, and download a high-quality PNG. Your photo never leaves your device.

howTo.title: How to use

Choose your target ID size and background color. Use the zoom and offset controls to frame the face correctly.
Download a high-quality PNG, ready to print or submit digitally.

tips.title: Tips for best results

Keep the face centered — zoom and offset controls fine-tune the composition.
White is the most common background for passport photos; check your destination country's requirements.

metadata.title: Image Denoise - Remove Noise from Photos Online
metadata.description: Free online tool to remove noise and grain from photos. Median filter algorithm with adjustable strength, processed entirely in your browser — private and secure.

image-denoise.title: Image Denoise
image-denoise.description: Automatically remove noise, grain, and compression artifacts from photos for a cleaner, sharper image. Uses a median filter algorithm that preserves edge detail well while denoising. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos are never uploaded.

faqs.question: How does denoising work?
faqs.answer: The tool uses a median filter algorithm: for each pixel, it takes the median value of its surrounding neighborhood as the new value. This effectively removes random noise and salt-and-pepper noise while preserving edges better than a mean blur.

faqs.question: What is noise?
faqs.answer: Noise is the randomly distributed grain or colored speckles in a photo, usually caused by high ISO, low-light conditions, or JPEG compression. Denoising can dramatically improve the quality of such photos.

faqs.question: Will denoising make my image blurry?
faqs.answer: A median filter preserves edges better than blur-based algorithms, but overly strong denoising can still lose some detail. Start with a small radius and increase it gradually if you are not satisfied.

faqs.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

upload.drop: Drop a photo or click to upload

whatIs.title: What Is the Image Denoise Tool?
body: The Image Denoise tool uses a median filter algorithm to automatically remove noise and grain from photos — ideal for high-ISO night shots, low-light captures, and heavily JPEG-compressed images.
A median filter removes noise while preserving edges and detail better than most approaches, making it a common denoising technique in photo editing.

howTo.title: How to Denoise an Image
items: Drop or upload the image you want to denoise.
Adjust the filter radius and strength as needed.
Click Denoise and wait for processing to finish.
Download the result as a PNG file.

tips.title: Tips
items: For noisy night photos, a 2px radius is a good starting point.
A strength of 100% uses the full filter result; lower values keep more of the original detail.
Denoise before upscaling to avoid amplifying noise along with the image.

metadata.title: Image Deblur - Sharpen Blurry Photos Online
metadata.description: Free online tool to sharpen blurry photos and restore crisp detail. Laplacian sharpening convolution with adjustable strength and iterations, processed entirely in your browser.

image-deblur.title: Image Deblur
image-deblur.description: Sharpen blurry or out-of-focus photos and restore detail and outlines. The tool uses Laplacian sharpening convolution with multiple iterations to make mildly blurred photos crisp again. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.question: How does deblurring work?
faqs.answer: The tool uses Laplacian sharpening convolution: it detects edges (high-frequency detail) in the image and re-adds that detail on top of the image. Multiple iterations gradually enhance clarity.

faqs.question: Can it fix severely blurred photos?
faqs.answer: It works well for mild to moderate blur and out-of-focus shots, but detail lost in heavily blurred photos cannot be recovered out of thin air. Start with a low strength to avoid halos and noise.

faqs.question: How should I set the parameters?
faqs.answer: Strength controls how much sharpening is applied per iteration (20–50% is recommended), and iterations controls how many rounds are applied (1–3 is recommended). Too much strength produces a halo effect.

faqs.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

upload.drop: Drop a photo or click to upload

whatIs.title: What Is the Image Deblur Tool?
body: The Image Deblur tool enhances image edges using Laplacian sharpening convolution, making mildly blurred, out-of-focus, or shaky photos crisp again.
Combined with multiple iterations, it gradually restores detail lost to blur — a convenient way to quickly fix blurry photos.

howTo.title: How to Deblur a Photo
items: Drop or upload a blurry photo.
Set a suitable strength and number of iterations.
Click Deblur and review the result.
Download the sharper version as a PNG file.

tips.title: Tips
items: Start with a strength of 30% and 1 iteration, then fine-tune from there.
Run the Image Denoise tool first to remove noise for better results.
White halos at high strength mean you have over-sharpened — lower the parameters.

metadata.title: Unsharp Mask - Online Image Sharpening Tool
metadata.description: Free online Unsharp Mask sharpening tool. The classic photography sharpening algorithm with adjustable amount and radius, processed entirely in your browser.

unsharp-mask.title: Unsharp Mask
unsharp-mask.description: Apply the classic photography sharpening algorithm — Unsharp Mask. It subtracts a blurred version from the original to get a detail mask, then blends it back in, giving precise control over sharpening amount and radius. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.question: What is an unsharp mask?
faqs.answer: Unsharp Mask is the most classic sharpening algorithm in photography: it applies a Gaussian blur to the image, subtracts the blurred version from the original to get a detail mask, then blends the mask back in by a set ratio. It gives precise control over the sharpening amount and radius.

faqs.question: What is the difference between amount and radius?
faqs.answer: Amount controls the sharpening intensity, i.e. how much of the detail mask is blended in; Radius controls the sharpening range, i.e. the size of the blur kernel used when detecting detail. Small radii enhance fine edges, while large radii affect wider edge regions.

faqs.question: Does sharpening damage image quality?
faqs.answer: Moderate sharpening makes photos look crisper, but too much amount produces white halos and noise that look unnatural. Try starting with an amount of 60–100%.

faqs.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

upload.drop: Drop a photo or click to upload

whatIs.title: What Is the Unsharp Mask Tool?
body: Unsharp Mask is a sharpening algorithm commonly used in professional software such as Adobe Photoshop. It boosts clarity by extracting and enhancing edge detail in the image.
Unlike simple convolution sharpening, Unsharp Mask offers independent amount and radius controls, giving more natural and controllable results.

howTo.title: How to Sharpen a Photo
items: Drop or upload the photo you want to sharpen.
Adjust the amount (sharpening intensity) and radius (sharpening range).
Click Sharpen to preview the result.
Download the sharpened image as a PNG file.

tips.title: Tips
items: For portraits, an amount of 60–80% with a radius of 2–3px is recommended.
For landscapes and architecture, you can increase the amount to 100%.
Sharpening is usually best done after color adjustments and resizing.

metadata.title: White Balance - Fix Photo Color Cast Online
metadata.description: Free online white balance correction tool. The gray-world algorithm automatically removes color casts and restores pure whites, processed entirely in your browser.

white-balance.title: White Balance
white-balance.description: Automatically correct color casts in your photos so whites return to pure white and colors look natural. The tool uses the gray-world algorithm to analyze the whole image and compute correction gains automatically — no need to pick a gray point by hand. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.question: What is white balance?
faqs.answer: White balance is the process of removing color casts from photos. Different light sources have different color temperatures, which can make photos look yellowish, bluish, or greenish. White balance correction makes white objects appear white in the photo.

faqs.question: How does the tool correct it?
faqs.answer: The tool uses the gray-world algorithm: it computes the average of the red, green, and blue channels across the whole image, then adjusts the channel gains so the three averages converge, neutralizing the color cast.

faqs.question: Which photos is it good for?
faqs.answer: It works well for photos taken under indoor incandescent (yellowish) or fluorescent (greenish) lighting, as well as photos with obvious color casts from sunsets or overcast days.

faqs.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

upload.drop: Drop a photo or click to upload

whatIs.title: What Is the White Balance Tool?
body: The White Balance tool automatically corrects color casts in photos — a quick fix for shots taken with incorrect white balance settings.

It uses the gray-world algorithm to analyze the colors of the whole image and automatically computes and applies the correction, with no need to pick a gray point or adjust color temperature manually.

metadata.title: Auto Contrast - Optimize Photo Depth Online
metadata.description: Free online auto contrast tool. Histogram stretching automatically optimizes the light and dark distribution with an adjustable clip ratio, processed entirely in your browser.

auto-contrast.title: Auto Contrast
auto-contrast.description: Optimize your photo's contrast and dynamic range in one click. The tool analyzes the image histogram, automatically stretches the light and dark distribution, and lets you clip extreme pixels to avoid blown-out highlights and crushed shadows. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.question: How does auto contrast work?
faqs.answer: The tool analyzes the image's brightness histogram, finds the actual darkest and brightest pixels, and stretches them across the full range (0–255), making the light and dark distribution fuller and giving the image more depth.

faqs.question: What does the clip ratio mean?
faqs.answer: The clip ratio decides how many extreme pixels are ignored. Setting it to 0.5% ignores the darkest and brightest 0.5% of pixels, preventing a few outliers (like specular highlights) from skewing the stretch.

faqs.question: Will it over-process my photo?
faqs.answer: The default 0.5% clip ratio is fairly gentle. If the image already has normal contrast, the stretch is minimal; low-contrast images see a clear improvement.

faqs.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

upload.drop: Drop a photo or click to upload

whatIs.title: What Is the Auto Contrast Tool?
body: The Auto Contrast tool uses histogram stretching to automatically optimize the light and dark distribution of an image, turning flat, hazy photos into clear ones with depth.
No need to adjust curves manually — one click gives you a fuller dynamic range.

howTo.title: How to Apply Auto Contrast
items: Drop or upload the photo you want to optimize.
Adjust the clip ratio as needed (0.5% by default).
Click Apply Auto Contrast and review the result.
Download the optimized image as a PNG file.

tips.title: Tips
items: Flat, hazy photos show the biggest improvement.
For photos with normal contrast, set the clip ratio to 0.
Combine with HDR Tone Mapping for even richer detail.

metadata.title: Histogram Equalization - Boost Image Contrast Online
metadata.description: Free online histogram equalization tool. Redistributes pixel brightness to bring out detail in shadows and highlights, processed entirely in your browser.

histogram-equalize.title: Histogram Equalization
histogram-equalize.description: Apply the histogram equalization algorithm to redistribute the brightness distribution of the image's pixels, stretching contrast in the luminance domain so that detail in both shadows and highlights becomes more visible. Adjustable strength, processed entirely locally in your browser.

faqs.question: What is histogram equalization?
faqs.answer: Histogram equalization remaps pixel brightness so the image's brightness histogram is more evenly distributed. It spreads brightness concentrated in a narrow range across the full range, significantly boosting contrast.

faqs.question: How is it different from auto contrast?
faqs.answer: Auto contrast only does a linear stretch, while equalization performs a non-linear mapping based on the cumulative distribution function. It uses the full brightness range more thoroughly and is especially good at enhancing detail in low-contrast images.

faqs.question: Will it introduce color casts?
faqs.answer: The tool equalizes the luminance (grayscale) channel while keeping each pixel's color proportions unchanged, so it will not introduce color casts.

faqs.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

whatIs.title: What Is the Histogram Equalization Tool?
body: Histogram equalization is a classic image enhancement algorithm. It redistributes pixel brightness to make the histogram more uniform, boosting overall contrast.
It is ideal for backlit, underexposed, or hazy photos, bringing hidden detail to light.

howTo.title: How to Equalize a Histogram
items: Drop or upload the photo you want to enhance.
Adjust the strength as needed (100% by default).
Click Equalize to see the result.
Download the enhanced image as a PNG file.

tips.title: Tips
items: Works best on low-contrast, hazy photos.
A strength around 50% gives a more natural look.
Noise may become more visible after processing — pair with Image Denoise if needed.

metadata.title: HDR Tone Mapping - Reveal High Dynamic Range Online
metadata.description: Free online HDR tone mapping tool. The Reinhard operator reveals highlight and shadow detail with adjustable exposure and strength, processed entirely in your browser.

hdr-tone-mapping.title: HDR Tone Mapping
hdr-tone-mapping.description: Apply the HDR tone mapping algorithm (Reinhard operator) to compress the light and dark differences of high-dynamic-range scenes, keeping highlights from blowing out and shadows full of detail. Adjustable exposure and strength, processed entirely locally in your browser.

faqs.question: What is HDR tone mapping?
faqs.answer: Tone mapping compresses the light and dark information of a high-dynamic-range (HDR) scene into a range that ordinary displays can show. The Reinhard operator applies non-linear compression to luminance, preserving detail in both highlights and shadows.

faqs.question: Does it work on ordinary photos?
faqs.answer: Yes. Even on a regular JPG, applying tone mapping makes highlights softer and shadow detail richer, producing an HDR-like look.

faqs.question: How should I understand the exposure parameter?
faqs.answer: Exposure mimics the exposure compensation used in HDR merging: raising it brightens shadows, while lowering it makes highlights more delicate. The default of 100% is neutral.

faqs.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

upload.drop: Drop a photo or click to upload

whatIs.title: What Is the HDR Tone Mapping Tool?
body: The HDR Tone Mapping tool uses the Reinhard operator to compress the image's luminance range, simulating the look of high-dynamic-range photography.
It makes highlights softer and shadow detail richer — ideal for backlit landscapes, night lights, and other scenes with a wide tonal range.

howTo.title: How to Apply HDR Tone Mapping
items: Drop or upload the photo you want to process.
Adjust the exposure and strength parameters.
Click Apply HDR Tone Mapping to review the effect.
Download the processed image as a PNG file.

tips.title: Tips
items: Backlit and night photos show the most dramatic improvement.
An exposure of 120–150% enhances shadow detail.
Too much strength makes the image look flat — keep it around 80–100%.

metadata.title: Dehaze - Remove Fog and Haze from Photos Online
metadata.description: Free online dehazing tool. The dark channel prior algorithm removes fog and haze to restore clear, crisp landscapes, processed entirely in your browser.

dehaze.title: Dehaze
dehaze.description: Remove fog, haze, and the low contrast they cause in your photos, restoring a clear and crisp scene. The tool uses the dark channel prior algorithm to estimate and compensate for atmospheric scattering. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.question: How does dehazing work?
faqs.answer: The tool uses the dark channel prior algorithm: it estimates the atmospheric light in the image, uses the dark channel to estimate the haze density (transmission) of each region, then reverses the atmospheric scattering to restore a clear scene.

faqs.question: Which photos is it good for?
faqs.answer: It works well on photos taken on foggy, hazy, or humid days, hazy-looking shots, and lightly misted mountain landscapes.

faqs.question: What does the window size mean?
faqs.answer: The window size is the local neighborhood range used when computing the dark channel, and it determines how finely the haze density is estimated. Larger windows give smoother estimates; smaller windows keep more detail.

faqs.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

whatIs.title: What Is the Dehaze Tool?
body: The Dehaze tool uses the dark channel prior algorithm to remove fog and haze from photos, restoring the scene's original clarity and color saturation.
It is ideal for fixing landscape photos taken on foggy or hazy days, making distant mountains and skies clear again.

howTo.title: How to Remove Haze from a Photo

For extremely dense fog, process twice for a more natural result.

image-rotate-flip.title: Rotate & Flip

faqs.question: Can I rotate at any angle?
faqs.answer: Yes. Besides the 90° quick buttons, a slider from -180° to 180° lets you rotate your image to any angle.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a horizontal flip and a vertical mirror?
faqs.answer: A horizontal flip mirrors the image left-to-right along the vertical axis (like a mirror), while a vertical mirror turns it upside down along the horizontal axis. The two can be combined.

faqs.question: Will rotation change the image size?
faqs.answer: Yes. When rotating at a custom angle, the output canvas expands to fit the rotated image, and the extra area is filled with a white background.

faqs.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your image never leaves your device.

metadata.title: Negative/Invert - Invert Image Colors Online
metadata.description: Free online tool to invert image colors for a film negative effect. One click, processed entirely in your browser.

image-negative.title: Negative/Invert
image-negative.description: Invert every pixel color in your image (255 minus the original value) for a film negative look. Black-and-white photos take on an X-ray quality, while color photos produce interesting complementary-color effects. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.question: What is the negative effect?
faqs.answer: The negative effect inverts every color in the image: black becomes white and white becomes black, with each color turning into its complementary color, just like a traditional film negative.

faqs.question: What is it good for?
faqs.answer: You can create X-ray-style black-and-white images, or give photos an artistic complementary-color look. Inverting again restores the original image.

faqs.question: Will I lose image information?
faqs.answer: No. Inversion is reversible — apply it again and the original colors come back.

faqs.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your image never leaves your device.

metadata.title: Pixelate/Mosaic - Pixelate Images Online
metadata.description: Free online tool to pixelate images for a mosaic or retro 8-bit look. Adjustable block size, processed entirely in your browser.

image-pixelate.title: Pixelate/Mosaic
image-pixelate.description: Average each region of your image into color blocks for a mosaic or retro pixel look. Adjust the block size to control the effect — small blocks give a retro 8-bit style, while large blocks are great for covering private details. All processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.question: What's the difference between mosaic and pixelate?
faqs.answer: They're essentially the same — both divide the image into color blocks. 'Mosaic' usually refers to large blocks (for covering details), while 'pixelate' refers to small blocks (for retro pixel art).

faqs.question: Can I use it to cover faces or private details?
faqs.answer: Yes. Set the block size large (32px or above) to cover faces, license plates, and other sensitive areas with color blocks.

faqs.question: How do I get a retro 8-bit style?
faqs.answer: Set the block size to 4–12px and keep the original colors — you'll get a pixel-art look like classic retro games.

faqs.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your image never leaves your device.

metadata.title: Oil Paint - Turn Photos into Oil Paintings Online
metadata.description: Free online tool to turn photos into oil paintings. Adjustable brush radius and color levels, processed entirely in your browser.

image-oil-paint.title: Oil Paint
image-oil-paint.description: Turn your photos into oil paintings. The algorithm counts the most frequent quantized color in each pixel neighborhood and paints with it, mimicking a painter's brushstrokes. Adjust the brush radius and color quantization level — all processing happens locally in your browser.

faqs.question: How does the oil paint effect work?
faqs.answer: The algorithm counts the most frequent quantized color in each pixel neighborhood and fills the center pixel with it, mimicking the smearing and blending of an oil painting brush.

faqs.question: What do radius and levels mean?
faqs.answer: Radius controls the brush size (larger means thicker strokes); levels control color quantization (fewer levels means simpler colors and a bolder style).

faqs.question: Which photos work best?
faqs.answer: Landscapes, still lifes, and portraits all work well. Photos with rich detail produce more vivid results — start with the default settings and adjust from there.

faqs.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your image never leaves your device.

metadata.title: Edge Detection - Extract Image Outlines Online
metadata.description: Free online edge detection tool. The Sobel operator extracts object outlines into a black-and-white line drawing, with adjustable threshold, processed entirely in your browser.

image-edge-detect.title: Edge Detection
image-edge-detect.description: Detect edges in your image with the Sobel operator to extract object outlines and create a black-and-white line-art effect. Adjust the threshold to control line density. All processing happens locally in your browser — your image is never uploaded.

faqs.question: How does edge detection work?
faqs.answer: The tool uses the Sobel operator to compute the brightness gradient of each pixel in the horizontal and vertical directions. Pixels with large gradients are edges, and the result is a black-and-white line drawing.

faqs.question: What does the threshold mean?
faqs.answer: The threshold decides which gradients count as edges: lower thresholds detect more lines, while higher thresholds keep only the most obvious outlines.

faqs.question: What is it good for?
faqs.answer: You can create line-art style images, extract object outlines for design reference, or use it as a sketch-style artistic filter.

faqs.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your image never leaves your device.

image-shadow.title: Drop Shadow
image-shadow.description: Add a soft drop shadow to your image so it looks more three-dimensional. The blur amount and horizontal/vertical offsets are all adjustable. All processing happens locally in your browser — your image is never uploaded.

faqs.question: What is a drop shadow?
faqs.answer: A drop shadow draws an offset, blurred dark outline behind the image to simulate the shadow cast by light, giving the image a sense of floating above its background.

faqs.question: What do blur and offset control?
faqs.answer: Blur controls how soft the shadow's edges are; the X/Y offsets control how far the shadow shifts horizontally and vertically.

faqs.question: What is it good for?
faqs.answer: It's great for web assets, product showcase images, and screenshot decoration that need a sense of depth.
